subject: Latency & 5xx Surge - Neptune Analytics - region steering & exec approval needed
messages:
From: Aaron Liu <aaron.liu@neptune-analytics.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Cc: Neptune Support <support@neptune-analytics.com>
Date: Thu, 16 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden latency + 5xx spike impacting batch scoring jobs

Aditya —

We started seeing a major latency and 5xx spike in our nightly batch scoring jobs around 02:30 UTC (us-east-1). P50 jumped from ~120ms to ~1.1s and token error rate rose to ~7% for several minutes; throughput dropped by ~40%. This is hitting several customer SLAs and downstream pipelines are retrying and amplifying load.

We attached a small set of traces and a short dashboard screenshot. Can Redwood steer traffic away from us-east-1a or fail us over to an alternate AZ/region while you investigate? We need immediate mitigation and an exec contact for credits if SLAs are breached.

Attachments: neptune-p50-p99-traces.zip (zip), dashboard-snapshot.png (image)

Please advise immediate next steps — Aaron
Aaron Liu
Head of Platform Engineering
Neptune Analytics
aaron.liu@neptune-analytics.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
To: Aaron Liu <aaron.liu@neptune-analytics.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 16 May 2028 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden latency + 5xx spike impacting batch scoring jobs

Aaron — thanks for the heads up and the traces. We've seen the spike in our alerts as well. I'm escalating to INFRA and our SE team immediately.

Short plan while we triage:
- Step 1 (now): Temporarily steer traffic for Neptune to us-west-2 (safe capacity) for the affected routes — this is a routing-level change and should be reversible within minutes.
- Step 2 (30–60m): Enable prefix/KV caching for the scoring workload where safe to reduce token compute during rollbacks.
- Step 3 (post-triage): Root-cause analysis + proposed credits if SLA impacted.

Ben — can you validate whether the model variant we serve for Neptune is available in us-west-2 quantized profile? If not, what's the deploy ETA for a compatible serving variant?

Marissa — looping you in for exec visibility and any guidance on credits or customer comms.

I'll confirm timing within 10 minutes.

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.ai

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, Aaron Liu <aaron.liu@neptune-analytics.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 16 May 2028 09:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden latency + 5xx spike impacting batch scoring jobs

Quick technical take after initial log pass:
- We see elevated contention and IO wait in us-east-1a on the host fleet serving the scoring route (correlated with a kernel upgrade rollout we observe in infra telemetry). Latency curvature and token-level 5xx aligns to intermittent kernel-level preemption.
- The model variant Neptune uses (redwood-gpt-medium-q4) is already available in us-west-2 in quantized form; the routing change should be non-disruptive provided we route only the scoring route (not stateful chat sessions).

Immediate asks/actions I can run now:
1) Push a targeted route override for /v1/generate?model=redwood-gpt-medium-q4 -> prefer us-west-2; will maintain sticky KV prefixes for scoring keys. Estimated flip < 5 minutes.
2) Warm cache for scoring prefixes in us-west-2 (background prefill) — ~15 minutes to reach steady p50.
3) Collect traces and a focused RCF (root cause fragment) for infra (I will attach logs).

If plumbing decides to fail traffic across regions we should also enable graceful retry caps to avoid retry amplification.

Attachments: sla-uptime-logset.zip

—Ben Carter
Staff Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 16 May 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden latency + 5xx spike impacting batch scoring jobs

Thanks team — good escalation. A few points from the exec bench:
- Authorize the cross-region steer immediately if Ben is confident the model variant and quant profiles are compatible. Prioritize minimizing customer impact.
- Prepare a succinct customer-facing note with timeline, what we changed, and what we're doing next. Aaron needs that for his execs.
- We should reserve the right to offer a one-time credit if we confirm SLA breach; finance has approved up to 30% one-off credits for critical incidents like these on enterprise deals. I'll need a short summary and a recommended credit amount to approve.

Lauren — please take the customer-facing summary and draft a comms email to Neptune (I trust you on tone).

Marissa Cole
VP, Customer Success
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: Aaron Liu <aaron.liu@neptune-analytics.com>, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 16 May 2028 10:19:00 -07:00
Subject: Customer update draft: Neptune Analytics — May 16 mitigation and next steps

Aaron —

We're preparing a short update for your execs while engineering finishes root cause analysis. Draft below — please let me know edits and we can send as soon as Ben confirms the steer is in place.

DRAFT:
Hi Aaron —

We detected a transient infrastructure regression impacting request latency and 5xx rates originating in us-east-1a. We have executed a routing steer to serve your scoring traffic from us-west-2 and are warming caches to restore steady throughput. Estimated timeline to steady-state: 15–45 minutes.

What we changed: routing override to us-west-2, cache prefill started, retry caps applied to avoid amplification.
What we're doing next: full RCA, targeted infra mitigation with our hosting partner, and impact analysis to determine SLA credit eligibility.

We will follow up with a detailed RCA and a recommended customer credit if an SLA gap is confirmed.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Customer Success Operations
lauren_bishop@redwood.ai

Please confirm and I'll send with the team tags.

From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai

Date: Sat, 18 May 2028 15:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Post-incident plan & exec next steps — Neptune Analytics (May 16)

Aaron — following up with a consolidated plan and ask from Redwood execs. Sorry for the delay in sending the wrap.

Summary of impact:
- Incident window: 2028-05-16T02:30:00Z - 2028-05-16T03:02:00Z (UTC)
- Observed p50 increase to ~1.1s, transient 5xx spike to 7%, throughput drop ~40% for scoring jobs.

Remediation performed:
- 09:42 PDT on 2028-05-16: routing override to us-west-2 for scoring routes; warm cache applied. Service returned to steady p50 within ~22 minutes.
- Scoped logs collected and submitted to infra for RCA. See attached sla-uptime-logset.zip and the internal trace bundle.

Executive asks / next steps:
1) Approve a one-time customer credit while we complete RCA. Recommended credit: 25% for the impacted billing period (recommended by CS + Finance as proportionate). We can sign the credit confirmation via the DocuSign link below.
2) Approve a postmortem customer briefing call with Neptune CTO and Redwood Infra lead (we propose Mon 2028-05-21 10:00 PDT).
3) Approve the infra mitigation plan to block kernel auto-upgrades on the serving fleet until compatibility validation completes (ops ask).

DocuSign link for credit confirmation: https://acct-redwood.docusign.com/NEP-CREDIT-2028
HubSpot record: https://hubspot.company/contacts/NEP-1234
Drive folder (RCA artifacts): https://drive.company/shared/neptune-esc-20280516

If these items look ok I'll route to Marissa for final approval and send the customer-facing note. Thanks for working through this with us — we'll keep you posted.

—Aditya
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
